title: Linear Combination of Vectors
notes: **Definition.** Given vectors v₁, …, vₙ and scalars x₁, …, xₙ, the vector r = x₁v₁ + … + xₙvₙ is a linear combination of them.
**Span.** The set of all linear combinations of v₁, …, vₙ is their span. In ℝ² two non-collinear vectors span the whole plane; in ℝ³ three non-coplanar vectors span all of space.
**Worked example.** Write (7, 1) as a combination of a = (1, 1) and b = (2, −1): x + 2y = 7 and x − y = 1 give y = 2, x = 3, so (7, 1) = 3a + 2b.
**Coefficient system.** Equating components turns r = x₁v₁ + … + xₙvₙ into a system of linear equations; solve by elimination, substitution, or Cramer's rule.
**Existence.** A solution exists iff r lies in the span. Geometrically, if a and b span a plane and r has a component out of that plane, no coefficients exist.
**Uniqueness.** Coefficients are unique exactly when the vectors are linearly independent; with dependent vectors, infinitely many coefficient sets produce the same r.
**Linear independence.** v₁, …, vₙ are independent when x₁v₁ + … + xₙvₙ = 0 forces every xᵢ = 0; otherwise one vector is a combination of the others.
**Basis.** An independent set that spans the space is a basis. In ℝ³ the standard basis is i, j, k, and (x, y, z) = xi + yj + zk with unique coefficients.

**Determinant test.** For three vectors in ℝ³, independence is equivalent to the determinant of the matrix with those vectors as rows (or columns) being non-zero; zero determinant means coplanar and dependent.
**Affine combinations.** When the coefficients sum to 1, the combination stays in the plane (or line) through the points; p = (1 − t)a + t b traces the segment AB as t runs from 0 to 1.
**Vector equation of a line.** r = a + t d is an affine combination of a point and a direction; the plane through a with directions d₁, d₂ is r = a + s d₁ + t d₂.
**Exam caution.** Do not assume a basis: check independence first. Three vectors with scalar triple product zero are coplanar, so they cannot represent every vector of ℝ³.
summary: A linear combination of vectors v₁, …, vₙ is any sum x₁v₁ + … + xₙvₙ with real coefficients. Two non-collinear vectors span a plane, three non-coplanar vectors span space; solving for the coefficients is solving a linear system, and uniqueness is exactly linear independence.
importantStatements: A vector lies in the span of v₁, …, vₙ exactly when the coefficient system is consistent.
Coefficients in a basis are unique.
Three vectors in ℝ³ are independent iff their scalar triple product is non-zero.
importantNotes: Independence controls uniqueness, not existence; a spanning set controls existence.
A set containing the zero vector is automatically dependent.
In ℝⁿ no more than n vectors can be linearly independent.
examShortTricks: Put the vectors as COLUMNS of a matrix and row-reduce the augmented system [v₁ … vₙ | r].
For two 2-D vectors, a non-zero determinant x₁y₂ − x₂y₁ immediately proves they span the plane.
If coefficients must sum to 1, add that equation to the system before solving.
formulas: span{v₁, …, vₙ} = { Σ xᵢvᵢ : xᵢ ∈ ℝ }
independence ⇔ Σ xᵢvᵢ = 0 ⇒ xᵢ = 0 for all i
det[v₁ v₂ v₃] ≠ 0 ⇔ {v₁, v₂, v₃} is a basis of ℝ³
p = (1 − t)a + t b,  0 ≤ t ≤ 1  (segment AB)
examples: Express (4, 5, 6) as a combination of i, j, k: (4, 5, 6) = 4i + 5j + 6k, with coefficients unique because the standard basis is independent.
Check whether (1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0) and (1, 1, 0) are independent. The determinant of [[1,0,0],[0,1,0],[1,1,0]] is 0, so they are coplanar and dependent: the third equals the sum of the first two.
practiceQuestions: Write (5, 3) as a linear combination of (1, 1) and (3, 1).
Determine whether (1, 2, 3), (0, 1, 2) and (0, 0, 1) form a basis of ℝ³.
Find t so that the point (1 − t)(2, 1) + t(6, 5) is the midpoint of the segment.
confusion: Thinking any two vectors span ℝ²; parallel vectors span only a line.
Assuming a representation is unique without first proving the vectors are independent.
practice: Solve three coefficient systems by row reduction and check each answer by re-substitution.
Find two different coefficient sets for the same vector using a dependent set.
universalFacts: Every vector space has a basis, and all bases of a given space have the same number of elements.
The dimension of ℝ³ is 3, so four vectors in ℝ³ are always dependent.
specialNotes: The section formula is an affine combination: coefficients n/(m+n) and m/(m+n) sum to 1.
Centroids use equal weights: the centroid of a triangle with vertices a, b, c is (a + b + c)/3.
examNotes: Write the coefficient equations explicitly before solving; method marks attach to that step.
State whether the representation is unique, and justify it with independence.

mcs.question: The vectors (1, 2) and (2, 4) span
mcs.explanation: The second is twice the first, so they are dependent and span only one direction.

mcs.question: Coefficients in the representation r = x₁v₁ + … + xₙvₙ are unique when
mcs.explanation: Independence makes the only representation of zero trivial, which forces uniqueness for every r in the span.
